rules.ekadashi: madhyahna-vyapini, both pakshas (24/yr): the LAST civil day whose NOON (12:00 NPT) falls inside the Ekadashi run; fallback the begin day. Discriminating receipt: Haribodhini Ekadashi printed 2026-11-20 though the tithi begins 07:31 NPT, after the sunrise (a strict udaya rule would print Nov 21).
rules.pradosham: trayodashi vyapta at SUNSET (pradosh kala = sunset -45 to +45 min), both pakshas (24/yr): the day whose sunset falls inside the Trayodashi run; fallback the begin day.
rules.sankashti_chaturthi: chandrodaya-vyapti: the day whose MOONRISE falls inside the Krishna Chaturthi run; when no moonrise falls inside, the day whose moonrise lies NEAREST the run (receipt: 2026-12-26 - no moonrise inside the 20:21 -> 17:29+1 run, the Dec 26 moonrise 19:56 sits 25 min before the begin against the Dec 27 moonrise 21:04, 3.6 h past the end; bhaktiras, hinducalendar.app and astrologger all print Dec 26). Neither HP nor BB prints a sankashti label (recorded absence) - the days are derived from their own tithi windows plus the BB moonrise and corroborated by the bhaktiras list.
rules.purnima_amavasya: the udaya day; vriddhi -> the FIRST udaya day (receipt: Kushmand Navami 2026-11-18, first of two).
rules.borderline: run edge within 30 min of a reference instant, two reference instants in one run, a fallback day, or (ekadashi) udaya divergence - convention-sensitivity, not engine doubt.

caveats.text: Neither Hamro Patro nor BhaktiBharat prints a sankashti chaturthi label on 2026-11-27 - a recorded publisher absence, not an engine doubt: the day is derived from their own printed tithi windows and the BhaktiBharat moonrise, and corroborated by the bhaktiras 2026 sankashti list (Nov 27 included, next Dec 26).

In the Nov 19-21 vriddhi stretch Hamro Patro's panel labels ride the begin-day tithi: on 2026-11-20 the panel reads Ekadashi while the Nepal Sambat line reads Dashami (the true udaya chain), and the flagged pages print the flagged tithi START in the samapti field. The vrat rules key on tithi runs, never on panel labels, so the shift cannot leak in.

The Indian portals name ekadashis by the udaya family: astrologger prints Rama Ekadashi on the udaya day Nov 5 2026 (noon day Nov 4) and Mokshada on the udaya day Dec 20 2026 (no noon inside that run); the Vijaya vriddhi (Mar 4 2027) is named on the second udaya day. The engine madhyahna rule reproduces every in-window receipt (Nov 20, Dec 4 - astrologger agrees on both); the out-of-window udaya rows are recorded, never absorbed.
The receipts confirm amanta month naming: Guru Nanak Jayanti on Kartik Purnima (2026-11-24) and Haribodhini on Kartik Shukla Ekadashi (2026-11-20), both inside amanta Kartika (Nov 10 - Dec 8 2026).

borderline marks convention-sensitivity (a run edge within 30 min of a reference instant, two reference instants in one run, a fallback, or ekadashi udaya divergence), never engine doubt: receipt-verified days exist in both states - the Nov 20 Haribodhini Ekadashi and the Dec 8 Aunsi are borderline, the Nov 22 / Dec 6 Ravi Pradosh, Nov 27 Sankashti, Nov 24 Purnima and Dec 4 Utpanna are not.

The Dec 26 2026 sankashti is the sink case of the sankashti rule: NO moonrise falls inside the chaturthi run (Dec 26 20:21 -> Dec 27 17:29). The BB moonrise prints (Dec 26 19:56, Dec 27 21:04) pin the nearest-moonrise fallback to Dec 26, and bhaktiras, hinducalendar.app (2026 list: Nov 27, Dec 26) and astrologger (New Delhi, moonrise 20:18 IST inside the 20:05 IST begin) all print Dec 26 - a Delhi/Kathmandu clock shift flips the run membership, not the day. The engine marks the day borderline (fallback + moonrise 25 min from the run edge).
